summary.para: Estimate the recall and cost of approximate kNN search configurations on a dense_vector field against a more thorough baseline. The field must use the bbq_disk index type, and must not be inside a nested object.

Each knn_settings entry reports the mean recall of the baseline's top k, not of relevance judgments, plus included and excluded query counts and cost totals. A query is excluded from the mean recall when the candidate finds a document scoring above the baseline's lowest top k score. A baseline returning fewer than k hits fails that query, because recall at k is undefined. All configurations run against one point in time.

The default baseline uses a visit_percentage of 20 and a rescore_vector.oversample of 100. An exact full-precision baseline must be requested explicitly with allow_exact_baseline, and is limited to 100 million vector-by-query comparisons.
The request is refused when the search.knn_eval.enabled cluster setting or the index.knn_eval.enabled index setting is false.
If true, the baseline can be exact. An exact baseline compares every vector at full precision, and can severely slow down other searches.

If false, the request returns an error if any wildcard expression, index alias, or _all value targets only missing or closed indices. This behavior applies even if the request targets other open indices.
The settings of the search that the knn_settings entries are compared with. If not specified, it uses a visit_percentage of 20 and a rescore_vector.oversample of 100.
The type of index that wildcard patterns can match. It supports comma-separated values, such as open,hidden.
If false, the request returns an error if it targets a missing or closed index.
A comma-separated list of index names to search.
The number of nearest neighbors to compute the recall for, from 1 to 1000.
The kNN search settings to evaluate, from 1 to 32 unique entries.
The source of the query vectors.

If true, the request waits for the evaluation to complete. A large evaluation can run for minutes, and closing the connection, for example because of a client or proxy timeout, cancels it. If false, the request returns a task identifier, and stores the completed response for retrieval through the task management API.
